rules.summary: US persons may not subscribe unless the board or management company decides otherwise. The prospectus defines 'US person' with its own list (US residents, US-organised entities, etc.) that ends with a Regulation S Rule 902 catch-all, and carves out 'Non-United States persons' under CFTC Rule 4.7, so the definition is mixed. The test is based on residence and incorporation, not citizenship: US taxpayers may subscribe if they are not US persons, so US citizenship alone does not exclude.

citations.quote: The shares in the SICAV may not be directly or indirectly offered or sold in the USA. Unless otherwise decided by the board or the management company, US persons may not subscribe for shares in the SICAV.

US persons do not include any “Non -United States person” as used in Rule 4.7 under the U.S. Commodity Exchange Act, as amended. Therefore, US taxpayers, as defined for US federal income tax purposes, may subscribe for shares in the SICAV as long as they do not qualify as US persons.
any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S

rules.summary: Jurisdiction restriction: shares may be offered or bought only where they are registered for public sale or where local law does not prohibit the sale. Some funds or classes are not available in every jurisdiction, so check registration in the client's country.

citations.quote: Distributing this prospectus, offering these shares for sale, or investing in these shares is legal only where the shares are registered for public sale or where sale is not prohibited by local law or regulation.
Also, some funds or share classes that are available in certain jurisdictions may not be available in others.

rules.summary: Discretionary gatekeeping: the SICAV may reject any subscription in whole or in part. It may also soft-close (to new investors) or hard-close a fund or share class without notice, and may compulsorily redeem holders who are not eligible.

citations.quote: Reject or cancel any application to open an account or any request to subscribe for or transfer shares We can reject the entire amount or part of it.
A closure may apply only to new investors (soft closure) or to further investments from existing shareholders as well (hard closure).

rules.summary: BI-EUR is core class I (accumulating), restricted to institutional investors. The prospectus defines these as investors under art. 174 of the 2010 Law: credit institutions and other financial professionals investing for themselves or for others (including retail clients under a discretionary management agreement), insurers, pension funds and UCIs. Contradiction: the BI-EUR KID says the fund is 'suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels', which conflicts with the class-level institutional restriction in the prospectus. Apply the prospectus restriction.
